messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Higher and further education, Social behaviour and attitudes, and Political behaviour and attitudes in Uruguay during the 1960s, matching this research need: student attitudes toward political, social, and economic issues, educational problems, views on the elite in the Third World, with demographic variables such as age, sex, religion, education, occupation, household status, and social class
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: Uruguay 1960s university students attitudes political social economic issues educational problems elites third world survey dataset
site:icpsr.umich.edu Uruguay students attitudes elite third world 1960
Uruguay student attitudes 1960s dataset survey political educational problems religion occupation
action.query: Uruguay 1960s university students attitudes political social economic issues educational problems elites third world survey dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Comparative National Development Project (Uruguay), 1966 — GESIS ZA0401","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0401","justification":"Excellent match to the research requirements. Conducted in Uruguay in 1966 under the direction of Seymour M. Lipset, this survey investigates university students' attitudes toward political, social, and economic issues, educational problems, and the role of elites in developing countries (the Third World). Topics include motivations for university enrollment, career aspirations, educational satisfaction, university functions, political involvement, political discussions, international affairs, and social values. The study includes demographic and socioeconomic background information useful for examining differences in attitudes. Its subject classifications explicitly cover higher education, social behaviour and attitudes, and political behaviour and attitudes. This is the closest match to the requested dataset."},{"title":"University Students' Values, Vocations, and Political Orientations: Uruguay, 1966 (ICPSR 7064)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.3886/ICPSR07064.v1","justification":"Excellent match. This 1966 survey of university students in Uruguay examines educational experiences, professional expectations, political orientations, social values, and attitudes toward national and international economic issues. Questions address agrarian reform, government intervention, foreign investment, Latin American economic integration, the Cuban Revolution, political participation, and student and faculty involvement in politics. Educational variables include secondary schooling, academic aspirations, university expectations, and parental and grandparental education. Demographic variables explicitly include age, sex, marital status, number of siblings, religion, and occupation. The dataset forms part of a comparative Latin American university student research project and is particularly suitable for investigating student attitudes, educational problems, and political orientations in developing societies. It appears to be an alternative archival version of the GESIS study listed above."},{"title":"Multi-National Student Survey, 1967–1968","url_or_doi":"https://b2find.eudat.eu/dataset/e1dadbf1-ea29-5758-ac9d-657486b6a416","justification":"Potentially relevant comparative dataset examining university students' political attitudes, social values, educational experiences, and perceptions of national and international problems during the late 1960s. The survey investigates student political participation, demonstrations, organizational membership, political ideology, religious beliefs, social progress, national priorities, and attitudes toward contemporary political issues. Background variables include age, sex, citizenship, university, field of study, anticipated occupation, father's occupation, family income relative to national income levels, and religious affiliation. Occupational and family-income information may support analysis of socioeconomic background and social class. However, the available description does not establish whether Uruguay was among the participating countries, so geographical coverage must be verified before using this dataset."},{"title":"Uruguay Public Opinion Survey Collection — Roper Center for Public Opinion Research","url_or_doi":"https://ropercenter.cornell.edu/featured-collections/uruguay","justification":"Useful supplementary source for historical political and social attitudes in Uruguay. The Roper Center identifies 19 Uruguayan survey datasets from the 1960s. Topics represented across its Uruguay collection include political preferences, electoral behaviour, government evaluations, economic conditions, international relations, and social conflict. These historical surveys may provide contextual evidence about public attitudes during the period when university students were becoming politically active. However, this is a collection landing page rather than a single student-focused dataset, and individual surveys must be examined to determine whether they include educational attitudes, student respondents, or the requested demographic variables."}]}
